subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
passage:
First week of June. Sarika, who had guided Lavanya through her first two years at the Jaipur software firm, invited her to lunch and insisted on splitting the bill. "We're colleagues now. Equal shares." Lavanya laughed, then realised it was true.
Mid-July. A new intern, Nikhil, froze during his first code review. Lavanya found him later by the water cooler and told him about her own disastrous first review, the one Sarika had talked her through.
Late August. Nikhil messaged Lavanya: "Merged my first feature!" She forwarded it to Sarika with a note: "Passing on what you gave me. Thank you." Sarika's reply was a single line: "That's the whole point 🎉"

qa.q: Where did Lavanya find Nikhil after his first code review?
qa.a: She found him by the water cooler.

qa.q: Why did Lavanya forward Nikhil's message to Sarika?
qa.a: She felt grateful and wanted Sarika to know that her help was now being passed on to someone newer.

qa.q: How did Lavanya pay forward what she received, and why did it work?
qa.a: She shared her own disastrous first review with Nikhil, just as Sarika once talked her through it, which eased his fear and helped him keep going.

qa.q: What does Sarika's reply show about how she sees the circle?
qa.a: Sarika sees mentoring as successful when help moves on to others, and seems proud rather than left behind.

grounding: Over a summer a mentee becomes her mentor's equal and starts guiding a new intern, thanking her mentor by passing the help on.

subtype: Stage 6: Peer and paying it forward [Response]
passage: Arohi, you say you feel strange now that the new trainee calls you 'ma'am'. Let your Dadi, Hansa, tell you something. When I was twenty-five, a nurse at the district hospital, Sister Kamala taught me everything, from finding a tiny vein to calming a frightened father at midnight. Two years later she started asking my opinion on the ward rota. One evening she said, 'Call me Kamala, not Sister.' We drank tea as friends after that, forty years of tea. That same winter a new girl, Mariam, cried in the linen room after losing her first patient. I sat with her the way Kamala once sat with me. When I thanked Kamala, she said, 'Don't thank me. Sit with the next one.' So, beti, sit with your trainee.

qa.q: Where did Mariam cry after losing her first patient?
qa.a: Mariam cried in the linen room.

qa.q: Why did Hansa sit with Mariam in the linen room?
qa.a: She remembered how Kamala had once sat with her and wanted Mariam to feel that same comfort; it was her way of carrying her gratitude forward.

qa.q: What is Dadi advising Arohi to do, and why?
qa.a: To sit with and guide her new trainee, because that is how the help Hansa received from Kamala keeps moving to the next person.

qa.q: How might Kamala have felt seeing Hansa guide Mariam?
qa.a: She would probably feel proud and content, since she saw thanks as best expressed by helping the next one.

grounding: A grandmother recalls her mentor becoming a friend of equals while she began guiding a newer nurse, passing the help on.
